text:
Maria Chen: Flagging a follow-up after today's spike: when ingress queueing hit ~300ms p99 we saw a spike in retry storms from customers who retried on opaque 502s. We need a more explicit contract for aborts vs resumable resets.
Vikram Patel: Agreed. Current gateway collapses client-abort, upstream-timeout, and internal throttling into 5xx. That makes clients retry heuristics brittle.
Ashley Jordan: Proposal: introduce a 4xx-ish transient code (we discussed 499 earlier) for client-initiated aborts and a separate "Reset-Resume" handshake: on detection of sustained backpressure, return 409+X-Resume-Offer header instead of hard abort.
Joel Rivera: 409 is odd semantically. Maybe 425 (Too Early) or 409 (Conflict) + clear header. Clients can opt-in to resume flow. We must define token semantics.
Maria Chen: Token draft: base64 of {node_id, upstream_checkpoint, stream_offset, ttl, hmac}. Example: X-Resume-Offer: resume=eyJub2RlIjoiZTFiIiwiY2hpIjoibm9uZSIsIm9mZnNldCI6IjEwMCJ9..
Ashley Jordan: Important: resume token MUST be bound to upstream commit id or kvcache checkpoint. Without that we risk replaying side-effects when the upstream already committed.
Vikram Patel: Implementation design notes: per-node resumestore as a small sharded in-memory LRU with configurable capacity. Recommend sharding by tenant to reduce hotspots. Config knobs: resume.enabled, resume.ttl_seconds, resume.max_entries_shard, resume.shards_per_node.
Joel Rivera: Rough resource calc: average token blob 256 bytes. 20k entries/node -> ~5MB. GC and probing adds CPU; justify with fewer end-to-end retries and lower peak upstream load.
Maria Chen: Observability: resume_offer_count, resume_accept_count, resume_reject_reason{stale,capacity,non_idempotent}, resume_resume_latency, resume_memory_bytes. Alert: resume_reject_ratio > 5% over 5m -> page SRE.
Ashley Jordan: Hedging interactions: If client accepts resume we must NOT trigger server-side hedges/dup upstream calls. Resume acceptance must include an upstream checkpoint id and the node must validate that the upstream has not progressed beyond that checkpoint. Otherwise reject.
Vikram Patel: Also add a fast-path: for idempotent read-only endpoints we can allow resume without upstream checkpoint if client supplies Idempotency-Key header and server confirms. But default should be conservative.
Joel Rivera: Security: tokens HMAC'd with node secret and include TTL. Rotation: include key-id in token and check against a keyring. Ops: when rotating keys, allow a grace window.
Maria Chen: Rollout plan: 1) Short-term (1 sprint) split error classes so client-abort -> 499, upstream-timeout -> 504, internal-throttle -> 429. 2) Mid-term (behind FF, Dedicated only) enable resume_offer on canary nodes. 3) Full rollout if metrics look good.
Ashley Jordan: Dev notes: API change minimal: add HTTP trailer/header X-Resume-Offer and X-Resume-Token. Client flow: on 4xx+X-Resume-Offer, client can call POST /v1/resume with header X-Resume-Token to continue stream. Server validates token and replays from upstream_checkpoint/offset.
Vikram Patel: Pseudocode for server resume validation: ```// validate token, check ttl & hmac if token.node != current_node reject if upstream_checkpoint != current_upstream_checkpoint reject unless idempotent_key present```
Joel Rivera: Operational guardrails: resume.store_usage_pct > 80% -> disable resume_offer nodewide and fall back to hard aborts. Also expose resume_store_count in console.
Maria Chen: Billing note: if resume avoids re-generating tokens on client side then billed token accounting needs to be tied to final upstream consumption. Finance must decide if we bill partial aborted tokens. Looping in billing.
ops-bot: Canary deploy scheduled: edge-runtime v2.15.0-canary to prod-canary @ 2026-03-25T03:00Z. Watch metric: resume_offer_count and 499/502 ratio.
Ashley Jordan: I'll open two PRs: (A) error-class split + hedging tweak, (B) stub resume headers + unit tests and feature flag gating.
Vikram Patel: I'll draft the resumestore proto and a small perf test. Joel, can you add the metrics to console mock?
Joel Rivera: On it. I'll add dashboard widgets and alert runbook notes.
Maria Chen: Thanks. Let's keep this thread for follow-ups. If anyone wants to riff on token format or shard sizing drop notes here. :thumbsup:
